ayahOccurrences.text: وَقَالَتِ ٱلْيَهُودُ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ نَحْنُ أَبْنَٰٓؤُا۟ ٱللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّٰٓؤُهُۥ ۚ قُلْ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُم بِذُنُوبِكُم ۖ بَلْ أَنتُم بَشَرٌ مِّمَّنْ خَلَقَ ۚ يَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ وَإِلَيْهِ ٱلْمَصِيرُ

ayahOccurrences.text: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا۟ ٱلْيَهُودَ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰٓ أَوْلِيَآءَ ۘ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ ۚ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّهُم مِّنكُمْ فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنْهُمْ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ

lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
ن/ص/ر   n–ṣ–r flood channels leading into a valley, tributaries of a river, rain falling on arid land
; to aid, to assist in repelling an attack, helpers, disciples; to triumph; to become impregnable; to avenge oneself. Philologists derive the word نَصْرَانِيٌّ naṣrāniyy from this root although it is more likely that the word is of Syriac origin derived from the name of Jesus’ hometown, Nazareth (النَّاصِِِرَة).

نَصَرَ naṣara 45 times; يُنْصَرُ yunṣar 14 times; تَنَاصَرَ tanāṣara 1 time; انْتَصَرَ ʾintaṣara 7 times; اسْتَنْصَرَ ʾistanṣara 2 times; نَصْرٌ naṣr 22 times; نَاصِرٌ nāṣir 3 times; نَاصِرُون nāṣirūn 8 times; أَنْصَارٌ ʾanṣār 11 times; نَصِيرٌ naṣīr 24 times; مَنْصُورٌ manṣūr 1 time; مَنْصُورُون manṣūrūn 1 time; مُنْتَصِرٌ muntaṣir 2 times; مُنْتَصِرُون muntaṣirūn 2 times; نَصْرَانِيٌّ naṣrāniyy 1 time and نَصَارَى naṣārā 14 times.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
يُنْصَرُ yunṣar [imperf. pass. v.]

1 to be assisted, to be given succour, to be aided

(3:111) وَإِنْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ يُوَلُّوكُمُ الأَدْبَارَ ثُمَّ لاَ يُنْصَرُونَ even if they fight you, they will turn tail; then they will not be helped

2 [with prep. مِن] to be delivered, to be saved

(23:65) لاَ تَجْأَرُوا الْيَوْمَ إِنَّكُمْ مِنَّا لاَ تُنْصَرُونَ do not cry out today–you will not be rescued from/by Us.

entries.label: ن-ص-ر
entries.definitionHtml:
ن/ص/ر   n–ṣ–r flood channels leading into a valley, tributaries of a river, rain falling on arid land
; to aid, to assist in repelling an attack, helpers, disciples; to triumph; to become impregnable; to avenge oneself. entries.label: يُنْصَرُ
entries.definitionHtml:
يُنْصَرُ yunṣar [imperf. pass. v.]

1 to be assisted, to be given succour, to be aided

(3:111) وَإِنْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ يُوَلُّوكُمُ الأَدْبَارَ ثُمَّ لاَ يُنْصَرُونَ even if they fight you, they will turn tail; then they will not be helped

2 [with prep. مِن] to be delivered, to be saved

(23:65) لاَ تَجْأَرُوا الْيَوْمَ إِنَّكُمْ مِنَّا لاَ تُنْصَرُونَ do not cry out today–you will not be rescued from/by Us.

entries.label: اسْتَنْصَرَ
entries.definitionHtml:
اسْتَنْصَرَ ʾistanṣara [v. X trans.] to seek assistance, to call upon someone for help

(28:18) فَإِذَا الَّذِي اسْتَنْصَرَهُ بِالأَمْسِ يَسْتَصْرِخُهُ and there he was, the one who had sought his help the day before, [again] crying out to him for help.

entries.label: انْتَصَرَ
entries.definitionHtml:
انْتَصَرَ ʾintaṣara [v. VIII intrans.] to be victorious, to defend oneself, to repel aggression; to avenge oneself

(42:41) وَلَمَنِ انْتَصَرَ بَعْدَ ظُلْمِهِ فَأُولَئِكَ مَا عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ there is no cause to act against anyone who defends himself after being wronged.

entries.label: تَنَاصَرُون
entries.definitionHtml:
تَنَاصَرُون tanāsarūn [imperf. v. VI, with the 2nd person prefix ﺘ elided] to assist one another, to come to one another’s rescue

(37:25) مَا لَكُمْ لاَ تَنَاصَرُونَ why do you not now support each other?

entries.label: مَنْصُورٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
مَنْصُورٌ manṣūr [pass. part., pl. مَنْصُورُون mansūrūn] one who is aided, assisted

(17:33) إِنَّهُ كَانَ مَنْصُورًا he is already aided [by God].

entries.label: مُنْتَصِرٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
مُنْتَصِرٌ muntaṣir [act. part., pl. مُنْتَصِرُون muntaṣirūn] one capable of defending himself

(18:43) وَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ فِئَةٌ يَنْصُرُونَهُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مُنْتَصِرًا he had no forces to help him other than God–he could not [even] help himself.

entries.label: نَاصِرٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَاصِرٌ nāṣir [act. part., pl. نَاصِرُون nāṣirūn and أَنْصَارٌ ʾanṣār] one giving assistance against an adversary

(61:14) كُونُوا أَنْصَارَ اللَّهِ be God’s helpers; *

(9:100) الْمُهَاجِرِينَ وَالأَنْصَارِ the Emigrants and the Helpers (the early Meccan Muslims who migrated from hostile Mecca to Yathrib–subsequently called Medina–and who became known as the Emigrants were well‐received by the Medinan Muslims who became known as the Helpers).

entries.label: نَصَرَ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَصَرَ naṣara u [v. trans.]

1 to assist, to aid, to succour

(3:160) إِنْ يَنْصُرْكُمُ اللَّهُ فَلاَ غَالِبَ لَكُمْ if God helps you, no one can overcome you

2 [with prep. مِن] to deliver, to save, to rescue, to help someone against someone or something

(21:77) وَنَصَرْنَاهُ مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا and We delivered him from the people who rejected Our signs.

entries.label: نَصِيرٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَصِيرٌ naṣır [intens. act. part.] staunch supporter, unwavering helper

(4:75) وَاجْعَل لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ وَلِيًّا وَاجْعَل لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ نَصِيرًا appoint for us a protector from your side and appoint for us a helper from your side.

entries.label: نَصْرٌ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَصْرٌ naṣr [v. n./n.] assistance, succour, aid

(8:72) وَإِنِ اسْتَنْصَرُوكُمْ فِى الدِّينِ فَعَلَيْكُمُ النَّصْرُ but if they seek help from you in the cause of faith, it is your duty to provide assistance; * النَّصْرُname of Sura 110, Medinan sura, so‐named because of the reference in verse

1 to God’s ‘Help’.

entries.label: نَصْرَانِيٌّ
entries.definitionHtml:
نَصْرَانِيٌّ naṣrāniyy [n., pl. نَصَارَى naṣārā] Christian

(5:69) إِنَّ الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالصَّابِئُونَ وَالنَّصَارَى مَنْ ءَامَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الآخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلاَ خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ those who believe [in the Message of Islam], the Jews, the Sabians and the Christians–all those who believe in God and the Last Day and do good deeds–there shall be no fear for them nor will they grieve.
